title: openai-compat: extend Responses API (seed/determinism, metadata passthrough) + streaming/tool-calling stability fixes
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: bring Redwood's OpenAI-compat Responses surface closer to parity with upstream Responses API variants by adding deterministic/seed flags, pass-through of user-provided metadata for response telemetry, and several fixes to streaming stability and function/tool-calling edges. This PR touches the compat adapter, runtime streaming paths, SDK wrappers, and tests. Summary of changes: 1) Responses adapter: add query params and request fields for 'seed' and 'deterministic' flags, ensure deterministic sampling/seed is threaded to runtime where supported, provide best-effort determinism warning when model/hardware does not guarantee bitwise reproducibility; 2) Metadata passthrough: preserve top-level request.metadata in generated Response objects and surface it in audit logs and telemetry hooks without mutating the user's payload; 3) Streaming stability: fix race condition in stream manager that could drop function/tool-calling payloads when a stream reconnect occurs; add backpressure accounting and idempotent stream resume tokens; 4) Function/tool calling: ensure structured output and tool-call signals follow OpenAI Responses semantics (choices[].tool_call vs choices[].message.function_call), normalize to a single canonical form in the compat layer and add a shim in SDKs; 5) Tests & docs: compatibility test matrix, new unit/integration tests exercising deterministic seeds and metadata passthrough, and docs updates for redwood-docs. Checklist: - [x] Add seed/deterministic fields to compatibility schema and request translation - [x] Thread seed to deterministic sampler where supported - [x] Add metadata passthrough plumbing and telemetry hook - [x] Fix stream resume race and add token accounting - [x] Canonicalize tool-calling/structured outputs for SDK consumption - [x] Add tests (unit + integration) - [x] Update docs and changelog Rollout plan: feature guarded behind 'openai_compat_v2' feature flag controlled via console; start with canary rollout to 5% hosted traffic and run compatibility evals and rerun downstream integration tests. If issues found, automatic fallback re-routes to previous compat adapter. Testing notes: ran unit tests and compatibility harness locally; added a regression integration test that replays an incident trace (INC-2026) to validate stream resume and tool-call signaling. Breaking changes: none expected — compat layer only extends request semantics and is opt-in. See release_notes for user-facing notes.
commits: Add seed/determinism fields to responses adapter
Thread seed into sampler and runtime adapter
Preserve request.metadata in response objects and telemetry
Fix stream resume race and add backpressure accounting
Normalize tool-calling outputs and add SDK shim
Add unit/integration tests and update docs
review_comments: Miguel Torres (review): Can you clarify how we warn customers when deterministic mode is not fully supported? Asha: added best-effort warning in adapter logs and surfaced a 'determinism_guarantee' field in response.metadata.

Ravi Singh (request changes): The stream resume token needed to be idempotent across reconnects; found a race in the previous approach. Asha: fixed by adding epoch+sequence resume token and added unit tests that simulate reconnects.
Eve Martinez (approve): Tests look good and coverage added for metadata passthrough. Asha: thanks, addressed minor nits around doc wording.

CI flake: the flaky test test_stream_resume was failing intermittently on linux-x86 GitHub runner; rerun of the job passed and I added tighter synchronization in the test harness to prevent future flakes.
Post-merge note from SRE: monitor streaming error rates and tool-call latencies during rollout; added a dashboard tile and alert (slo-toolkit) to catch regressions.
release_notes: Added seed/deterministic flags and metadata passthrough to OpenAI Compat Responses adapter (opt-in via openai_compat_v2 flag). Improved streaming resume reliability and normalized tool-calling outputs for SDKs. See docs/openai-compat/responses-v2.md for migration details.
